title: Coefficient projection cocycle for ordinary derived ringed diagrams
statement:
Let $u:\mathscr X\to\mathscr Y$ be a morphism of topoi presented by small sites [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism, def-weil-size-convention]. On $\mathscr Y$ fix composable homomorphisms $A\xrightarrow{a}B\xrightarrow{b}C$ of sheaves of commutative rings. On $\mathscr X$ use their inverse images $A_X,B_X,C_X$, including the induced ring maps. Use ordinary unbounded derived categories of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category], K-flat derived scalar extension [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], and the canonical derived inverse-image/direct-image adjunctions [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact]. Write $S_a^T=-\otimes^L_{A_T}B_T$, $S_b^T=-\otimes^L_{B_T}C_T$, $S_{ba}^T=-\otimes^L_{A_T}C_T$ for $T=X,Y$, and $G_D=Ru_{*,D}$ for $D=A,B,C$. Let $\tau_T:S_b^TS_a^T\xrightarrow{\sim}S_{ba}^T$ be balanced tensor associativity [lem-sfb-successive-derived-quotient-normalization].

Define $\chi_a:S_a^YG_A\to G_BS_a^X$ to be the $u_B^{-1}\dashv G_B$-adjunct of
$$u_B^{-1}S_a^YG_AM\xrightarrow{\sim}S_a^Xu_A^{-1}G_AM\xrightarrow{S_a^X\varepsilon_{A,M}}S_a^XM,$$
using the canonical inverse-image/tensor comparison; define $\chi_b,\chi_{ba}$ in the same way. Then the following identity of natural transformations holds:
$$\chi_{ba}\circ\tau_YG_A=G_C\tau_X\circ(\chi_bS_a^X)\circ S_b^Y\chi_a.$$
For an identity coefficient map $\chi$ is the identity under multiplication by the coefficient unit. Consequently, if a commutative square of coefficient ring sheaves $A\to B$, $A\to C$, $B\to D$, $C\to D$ has equal composites $A\to D$, the two successive projection comparisons to $D$ agree under their balanced tensor identifications. These equalities are natural in the ring maps, commute with the canonical cochain shifts, and hold in the target coefficient derived category. No flatness or invertibility of any $\chi$ is assumed.

The same assertions hold on the ordinary derived categories of strict inverse systems of module sheaves for compatible maps of ring systems: use the ringed diagram topoi of [lem-weil-pbc-diagram-site-realization] and the operations of [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. The identities are identities there before evaluation or total inverse limit.

source.place: Tag 0E47, remark-compose-base-change-horizontal (horizontal composition of the base change maps of Tag 07A7, remark-base-change), applied to the coefficient-change morphisms of ringed topoi $(\mathscr T,C_T)\to(\mathscr T,B_T)\to(\mathscr T,A_T)$ over $u$, whose base change maps are the $\chi$ of the statement and whose pullback composition is balanced associativity $\tau$; Tag 0D6E, lemma-derived-pushforward-composition, for the ordinary derived adjunctions. Stacks omits the verification; the unit clause, the diagram-topos clause and the shift clause are agent supplements. Motivation: Bhatt–Scholze 6.7.16–6.7.17.

proof.text: Put $A_Y=A$, $B_Y=B$, $C_Y=C$. For $D=A,B,C$ set $L_D=u_D^{-1}:D(D_Y)\to D(D_X)$ and $G_D=Ru_{*,D}:D(D_X)\to D(D_Y)$. These are the canonical derived pullback/direct-image adjunctions $L_D\dashv G_D$, with unit $\eta_D$ and counit $\varepsilon_D$. The module pullback formula is $D_X\otimes_{u^{-1}D_Y}u^{-1}(-)$, and its derived version tensors over the ring $u^{-1}D_Y$ on $\mathscr X$. Since $D_X=u^{-1}D_Y$, this is just the exact coefficient inverse image. In particular there is no tensor over $D_Y$ on $\mathscr X$. The cited K-flat preservation theorem applies to these ringed morphisms and also to identity-topos coefficient changes; thus all ensuing compositions of derived pullbacks can be computed on one K-flat flat-term representative.

source.place: Tags 07A6 (lemma-adjoint), 0G7E (lemma-pullback-K-flat); coefficient inverse images have their specified ring identifications

proof.text:
For $a:A\to B$ the two composites of ringed-topos morphisms from $(\mathscr X,B_X)$ to $(\mathscr Y,A_Y)$ agree: their ring map is $u^{-1}a$. The canonical derived pullback-composition comparisons therefore give an isomorphism
$$c_a:L_BS_a^Y\xrightarrow{\sim}S_a^XL_A$$
of functors $D(A_Y)\to D(B_X)$. Apply the cited composition-comparison theorem to the two paths through $(\mathscr Y,B_Y)$ and $(\mathscr X,A_X)$; its last clause supplies the identification of their equal composite morphisms. Its K-flat description identifies $c_a$ with the inverse-image/balanced-tensor comparison: for a K-flat flat-term $P$, both sides are canonically $u^{-1}P\otimes_{A_X}B_X$, as complexes of $B_X$-modules. The tensor-pullback theorem ensures that each pullback of $P$ is still an admissible K-flat flat-term complex. Define $c_b,c_{ba}$ in the same way. These are isomorphisms in the changed coefficient category, not merely after restriction of scalars.

Use the cited balanced scalar associator $\tau_T:S_b^TS_a^T\cong S_{ba}^T$, represented by $(x\otimes s)\otimes t\mapsto x\otimes b_T(s)t$. On a K-flat flat-term representative the comparisons of Step 2 only identify inverse image of a tensor with tensor of inverse images. Thus both composites from $L_CS_b^YS_a^Y$ to $S_{ba}^XL_A$ send a double tensor $(x\otimes s)\otimes t$ to $x\otimes b_X(s)t$, after the inverse-image identifications. They give the equality
$$(\tau_XL_A)\circ(S_b^Xc_a)\circ(c_bS_a^Y)=c_{ba}\circ(L_C\tau_Y).$$
This is an equality of $C_X$-linear chain maps on the common representative, hence in $D(C_X)$. The cited comparisons are computed on these representatives, so this verifies their coherence rather than assuming it. The same formulas show that $c_{\mathrm{id}}=1_{L_A}$ under scalar multiplication unitors and that the comparisons are natural in the ring maps.

source.place: Tag 0D6D (lemma-derived-pullback-composition); explicit double-tensor calculation with the associator

proof.text:
Apply the definition of an adjunction mate with $L_1=L_A$, $R_1=G_A$, $L_2=L_B$, $R_2=G_B$, $G=S_a^Y$, $H=S_a^X$, and square $\alpha=c_a:L_BS_a^Y\to S_a^XL_A$. Its mate has component
$$S_a^YG_AM\xrightarrow{\eta_{B,S_a^YG_AM}}G_BL_BS_a^YG_AM\xrightarrow{G_B(c_{a,G_AM})}G_BS_a^XL_AG_AM\xrightarrow{G_BS_a^X(\varepsilon_{A,M})}G_BS_a^XM.$$
Its transpose under precisely $L_B\dashv G_B$ is $S_a^X(\varepsilon_{A,M})\circ c_{a,G_AM}$, the composite defining $\chi_a$ in the statement. Thus $\chi_a=c_a^\flat$. The same substitution identifies $\chi_b=c_b^\flat$ and $\chi_{ba}=c_{ba}^\flat$. No composite such as $S_a^XL_A$ is being asserted to have right adjoint $G_B$.

source.place: Tag 07A7 (remark-base-change); the defining mate formula with the actual source and target adjunctions

proof.text:
Apply clause (1), pasting along $G,H$, of the cited mate theorem with $L_1=L_A$, $L_2=L_B$, $L_3=L_C$, their right adjoints $G_A,G_B,G_C$, and $G=S_a^Y$, $H=S_a^X$, $G_2=S_b^Y$, $H_2=S_b^X$, $\alpha=c_a$, $\beta=c_b$. It states that
$$\gamma=(S_b^Xc_a)\circ(c_bS_a^Y):L_CS_b^YS_a^Y\to S_b^XS_a^XL_A$$
has mate $\zeta=(\chi_bS_a^X)\circ S_b^Y\chi_a$. To include the associators explicitly, transpose the two desired maps under $L_C\dashv G_C$. By the mate definition and naturality of the counit, the transpose of $G_C\tau_X\circ\zeta$ at $M$ is
$$\tau_{X,M}\circ S_b^XS_a^X(\varepsilon_{A,M})\circ\gamma_{G_AM}.$$
Naturality of $\tau_X$ and Step 3 turn this into
$$S_{ba}^X(\varepsilon_{A,M})\circ c_{ba,G_AM}\circ L_C(\tau_{Y,G_AM}),$$
which is the transpose of $\chi_{ba,M}\circ\tau_{Y,G_AM}$. The adjunction bijection proves equality in $D(C_Y)$, giving the stated cocycle. Clause (2), which instead composes adjunctions, is not used.

source.place: Tag 0E47 (remark-compose-base-change-horizontal), verification by clause (1) of mate pasting and the adjunction bijection

proof.text: For an identity coefficient map, Step 3 gives the square $c_{\mathrm{id}}=1_{L_A}$. Its transpose at $M$ is $\varepsilon_{A,M}:L_AG_AM\to M$, which need not be an identity. The mate formula gives $G_A(\varepsilon_{A,M})\circ\eta_{A,G_AM}=1_{G_AM}$ by the triangle identity, equivalently clause (4) of the cited mate theorem. Thus $\chi_{\mathrm{id}}=1_{G_A}$ under the scalar unitors. For a commutative square of coefficient rings, apply Step 5 to each path $A\to B\to D$ and $A\to C\to D$. After the respective balanced tensor identifications both maps equal $\chi_{A\to D}$; their equality follows because the composite ring homomorphisms are equal. The associators are natural in those maps by the cited normalization theorem, so this is the specified square identity, with no choice of identification.

source.place: Tag 0E47 (remark-compose-base-change-horizontal); identity from the adjunction triangle identity, square from the two factorizations

proof.text: Check shifts before taking mates. Scalar extension by a ring sheaf uses that ring in cochain degree zero. For every integer $n$, on a K-flat representative its shift comparison is the chain identification $P[n]\otimes_A B\cong(P\otimes_A B)[n]$; both differentials are $(-1)^n(d_P\otimes1)$. Exact inverse image has the same termwise shift identification. The maps $c_a,c_b,c_{ba}$ of Step 2 only identify these tensors, and $\tau_T$ sends $(x\otimes s)\otimes t$ to $x\otimes b_T(s)t$ with $s,t$ in degree zero. Neither moves a positive-degree factor past another. Therefore these chain maps commute with the canonical shifts, within $D(B_X)$, $D(C_X)$, and the corresponding categories on $Y$. The cited K-flat computation and scalar normalization identify these chain maps with the actual derived comparisons, so this check does not use a claim that restriction of scalars detects equality.

source.place: Tags 0G7E (lemma-pullback-K-flat), 0D6D (lemma-derived-pullback-composition); direct cochain-shift calculation for degree-zero coefficient tensors

proof.text: For each $D=A,B,C$, the derived-adjunction shift theorem applies to the ringed morphism $(\mathscr X,D_X)\to(\mathscr Y,D_Y)$, including the target coefficient adjunction $L_B\dashv G_B$ (or $L_C\dashv G_C$). It states that both its unit and its counit commute with every canonical integer shift. Now the formula of Step 4 expresses $\chi_a$ as $G_BS_a^X\varepsilon_A\circ G_B(c_aG_A)\circ\eta_BS_a^YG_A$. Step 7 supplies shift compatibility of $S_a^X,S_a^Y,c_a$, and the cited theorem supplies it for $\eta_B,\varepsilon_A$ and the adjoint functors. Composing their shift squares proves $s_{G_BS_a^X}\chi_{a,M[n]}=\chi_{a,M}[n]s_{S_a^YG_A}$ as an equality in $D(B_Y)$. Repeat with $b,ba$ and combine with Step 7 for $\tau$. Hence the cocycle and square equalities respect shifts in their target coefficient categories. Naturality follows from the displayed mate formula, naturality of units/counits, and the representative formulas of Steps 2–3. No step requires flatness of the coefficient maps or invertibility of a mate.

source.place: Tag 07A6 (lemma-adjoint); canonical derived-adjunction shifts applied separately at every coefficient, followed by composition of the displayed shift squares

proof.text: For strict inverse systems use the small inverse-sequence indexing category and its diagram topos. The diagram-site realization and the system-sections lemma identify a strict system with a module over the corresponding ring object there, and supply the morphism $u_\bullet$ of diagram topoi, its inverse image and derived direct image, and the derived scalar-extension operations for compatible ring-system maps. Apply Steps 1–8 directly on these two small ringed diagram topoi with ring objects $A_\bullet\to B_\bullet\to C_\bullet$. The system lemma identifies their specified exchange maps with precisely the adjunction-mate words used here, and their units, counits and scalar tensors with the specified system operations. Thus the transposition and double-tensor calculations prove identities of maps in $D(\mathscr S(C))$ itself, including shifts there. The lemma also says evaluation agrees with these constructions, but equality is already proved before evaluation. No claim that evaluations detect equality of arbitrary derived morphisms, and no passage through total inverse limit, is used.
